_meta.note: Curated external inputs (values + 1σ uncertainties + context). Keep this small and auditable.
_meta.accuracy_notes: Values verified against primary sources (NIST web database, PDG PDF). Entries with 'CAUTION' or 'BROAD' in scheme field have larger-than-typical ambiguities. The PDG 2024 physical constants table still cites CODATA 2018 for alpha (noting CODATA 2022 update pending); we use CODATA 2022 here.

alpha_inv_mZ.scheme: MSbar 5-flavor inverse EM coupling at mZ; CAUTION: scheme-dependent -- differs from on-shell running (~128.9) by ~1 unit due to MSbar subtraction terms. The specific value depends on alpha_s(mZ) and the hadronic vacuum polarization input.
alpha_inv_mZ.citation: PDG RPP 2024 Electroweak review Sec.10.2.2: alpha_hat^{-1}(5)(MZ)=127.930+/-0.008

mW_GeV.scheme: pole mass; PDG world average (excl. CDF II); CAUTION: CDF II (2022) reported mW=80.4335±0.0094 GeV, 3.6σ above this average. The PDG excludes CDF II due to 0.5% compatibility probability when included. CMS (2024) reports mW=80.3602±0.0099 GeV, consistent with non-CDF average.
mW_GeV.citation: PDG RPP 2024 (mW); LHC-TeV MW WG combination excl. CDF II; see also CDF II: PRL 129 (2022) 121801

delta_alpha_lept_mZ2.scheme: leptonic vacuum polarization contribution at mZ^2 (approx)

delta_alpha_had5_mZ2.scheme: on-shell hadronic vacuum polarization (5 flavors) at mZ^2; CAUTION: this quantity is actively contested -- dispersive (e+e-) evaluations give ~0.02760, lattice QCD (Cè et al.) gives ~0.02773, and the PDG 2024 EW review (MS-to-on-shell conversion) gives 0.02783. The spread directly affects alpha(mZ) and is correlated with the muon g-2 tension.
delta_alpha_had5_mZ2.citation: PDG RPP 2024 Electroweak review Table 10.1: Delta alpha_had^(5)(MZ)=0.02783+/-0.00006 (updated with more precise charm quark mass; see also Davier et al. 0.02760+/-0.00010, Keshavarzi et al. 0.02761+/-0.00011)

delta_alpha_top_mZ2.scheme: top vacuum polarization contribution at mZ^2 (approx)

sin2thetaW_mZ_MSbar.scheme: MSbar weak mixing angle at mZ; CAUTION: scheme-dependent -- the MSbar value (0.23129) differs from the on-shell value (~0.2232) and the effective leptonic Z-pole value (~0.23153). These are NOT interchangeable; each is a valid sin2thetaW in a different renormalization convention. The PDG 2024 global fit value sin2theta_eff_lept=0.23153(4) corresponds to s_hat^2(MSbar)=0.23129(4) via radiative corrections.
sin2thetaW_mZ_MSbar.citation: PDG RPP 2024 Physical Constants Table: sin^2 theta_hat(MZ) (MS) = 0.23129(4)

sin2thetaW_on_shell.scheme: on-shell weak mixing angle (pole-mass definition); sin^2(thetaW)=1-mW^2/mZ^2
sin2thetaW_on_shell.citation: derived from PDG RPP 2024 mW and mZ

tgt_sin2thetaW(Qweak).scheme: sin2thetaW_eff: PV ep (Qweak final); inferred from Q_W^p at Q^2=0.0248 GeV^2 (space-like), using SM radiative corrections
tgt_sin2thetaW(Qweak).citation: Qweak Collaboration (Androic et al.), Nature 557, 207 (2018) (proton weak charge Q_W^p=0.0719±0.0045; DOI:10.1038/s41586-018-0096-0)

tgt_sin2thetaW(E158).scheme: sin2thetaW_eff: PV Møller (E158); quoted at Q^2=0.026 GeV^2 (space-like)

tgt_sin2thetaW(nue_lowE).scheme: sin2thetaW_eff: PV low-energy nu-e scattering global fit (reactor+accelerator); MeV-scale; single-Q approximation; BROAD (sigma/value~10%): very broad uncertainty makes this a weak constraint
tgt_sin2thetaW(nue_lowE).citation: arXiv:1608.02671 ("The weak mixing angle from low energy neutrino measurements: a global update")

tgt_sin2thetaW(CHARMII).scheme: sin2thetaW_eff: nu_mu-e scattering (CHARM II); sin^2Theta_{nu e} from differential cross-section ratio; representative Q^2~0.01 GeV^2 (Q~0.1 GeV); BROAD (sigma~3.6%): limited statistics from 1990s detector
tgt_sin2thetaW(CHARMII).citation: CHARM II Collaboration (P. Vilain et al.), Phys. Lett. B335 (1994) 246-252: sin^2Theta_{nu e}=0.2324+-0.0083

tgt_sin2thetaW(NuTeV).scheme: sin2thetaW_on_shell: NuTeV nu_mu-N DIS extraction (Paschos-Wolfenstein style); CAUTION (known anomaly ~3σ above SM): debated for decades -- possible explanations include strange-sea asymmetry (s vs sbar PDFs), isospin-violating effects, and nuclear shadowing corrections. Davidson et al. Eq.(9): s_W^2=0.2276±0.0013(stat)±0.0006(syst)±0.0006(th) -0.00003(Mt/GeV-175)+0.00032 ln(mh/100 GeV). Stored value applies mass correction with mt=172.57, mH=125.11. Representative DIS scale Q^2~20 GeV^2 (Q~4.47 GeV)
tgt_sin2thetaW(NuTeV).citation: Davidson, Forte, Gambino, Rius, Strumia (CERN-TH/2001-366), hep-ph/0112302 (NuTeV discussion; Eq.(9) quote)

tgt_sin2thetaW(NuTeV_eq10).scheme: sin2thetaW_on_shell: NuTeV alternative extraction from g_L^2,g_R^2 (Davidson et al. Eq.(10)) on the same page as Eq.(9): s_W^2(NuTeV)=0.2272±0.0017±0.0001(top)±0.0002(Higgs). sigma stored is quadrature-combined (0.0017146…≈0.0017). Representative DIS scale Q^2~20 GeV^2 (Q~4.47 GeV)
tgt_sin2thetaW(NuTeV_eq10).citation: Davidson, Forte, Gambino, Rius, Strumia (CERN-TH/2001-366), hep-ph/0112302 (NuTeV discussion; Eq.(10) quote)

tgt_sin2thetaW(CsAPV).scheme: sin2thetaW_eff: Cs-133 atomic parity violation (APV); E→0 effective limit; scheme of Ref. [31] in Porsev et al.; CAUTION: extracting sin2thetaW from APV requires precise many-body atomic theory calculations. Different groups give systematically different results (cf. CsAPV vs CsAPV_PDG entries; spread ~0.003)

tgt_sin2thetaW(CsAPV_PDG).scheme: sin2thetaW_eff: Cs atomic parity violation (APV) as low-energy weak mixing angle point; PDG quote at 2.4 MeV; CAUTION: differs from CsAPV entry (0.2381 vs 0.2349) due to different atomic structure theory and scheme conventions -- the spread reflects theoretical systematics in interpreting the same Cs APV measurement
tgt_sin2thetaW(CsAPV_PDG).citation: PDG RPP 2025 (Standard Model review, rpp2025-rev-standard-model.pdf): s_hat^2(2.4 MeV)=0.2349+/-0.0018 (Cs APV)

tgt_sin2thetaW(eDIS).scheme: sin2thetaW_eff: polarized electron-deuteron DIS (eDIS; SLAC E122 + JLab Hall A); PDG quote; representative DIS#1 scale Q^2≈1.085 GeV^2; BROAD (sigma~1.9%): dominated by systematic/statistical limitations of the vintage SLAC E122 data
tgt_sin2thetaW(eDIS).citation: PDG RPP 2025 (Standard Model review, rpp2025-rev-standard-model.pdf): s_hat_Z^2=0.2299+/-0.0043 (eDIS)

tgt_sin2thetaW(LEP_SLC_Zpole).scheme: sin2thetaW_eff_lept: Z-pole effective leptonic weak mixing angle sin^2θ_eff^lept = 1/4 (1 - v_l/a_l), from LEP+SLC Z-resonance observables; incorporates full EW radiative corrections; Q≈mZ
tgt_sin2thetaW(LEP_SLC_Zpole).citation: ALEPH+DELPHI+L3+OPAL+SLD + LEP EWWG + SLD EWWG, hep-ex/0509008 (updated 2006), Phys. Rept. 427 (2006) 257-454, doi:10.1016/j.physrep.2005.12.006: sin^2θ_eff^lept=0.23153±0.00016

tgt_sin2thetaW(Tevatron_Zpole).scheme: sin2thetaW_eff_lept: Tevatron Run II (CDF+D0) Drell–Yan forward-backward asymmetry extraction of sin^2θ_eff^lept at the Z pole; incorporates SM radiative corrections; Q≈mZ
tgt_sin2thetaW(Tevatron_Zpole).citation: Tevatron Run II combination of sin^2θ_eff^lept from CDF+D0 Drell–Yan A_FB, sin^2θ_eff^lept=0.23148±0.00033 (combined 9–10 fb^-1 per experiment; 2001–2011)

tgt_sin2thetaW(CMS_mW_2024).scheme: sin2thetaW_on_shell: derived on-shell weak mixing angle from CMS mW=80.3602±0.0099 GeV (2024) and PDG mZ=91.1880 GeV
tgt_sin2thetaW(CMS_mW_2024).citation: CMS Collaboration, CMS-PAS-SMP-23-002 (2024): mW=80360.2±9.9 MeV; sin2thetaW=1-mW^2/mZ^2

tgt_mp_over_me.scheme: proton-to-electron mass ratio (dimensionless; CODATA 2022); verified directly from NIST database

tgt_mmu_over_me.scheme: muon-to-electron mass ratio (dimensionless; CODATA 2022); verified directly from NIST database

tgt_mt_over_mW.scheme: top/W mass ratio (pole masses); sensitive to EW symmetry breaking dynamics
tgt_mt_over_mW.citation: derived from PDG RPP 2024: mt=172.57(29) GeV, mW=80.3692(133) GeV

tgt_mW_over_mZ.scheme: W/Z mass ratio = cos(thetaW); fundamental EW structure constant
tgt_mW_over_mZ.citation: derived from PDG RPP 2024: mW=80.3692(133) GeV, mZ=91.1880(20) GeV

tgt_mt_over_mb.scheme: top/bottom mass ratio (mt pole / mb MSbar at mb); probes Yukawa hierarchy
tgt_mt_over_mb.citation: derived from PDG RPP 2024: mt=172.57(29) GeV, mb(MSbar)=4.183(7) GeV

tgt_mb_over_mtau.scheme: bottom/tau mass ratio (mb MSbar at mb / mtau pole); famous near-equality at GUT scale in SU(5)-type unification
tgt_mb_over_mtau.citation: derived from PDG RPP 2024: mb(MSbar)=4.183(7) GeV, mtau=1.77686(12) GeV

tgt_mtau_over_mmu.scheme: tau/muon mass ratio; probes lepton mass generation mechanism
tgt_mtau_over_mmu.citation: derived from PDG RPP 2024: mtau=1.77686(12) GeV, mmu=0.1056584 GeV
